question_stem: A sample of a radioactive isotope emits a beam of β^{-} radiation.
question_stem_latex: A sample of a radioactive isotope emits a beam of $β^{-}$ radiation.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question_text:
State the change, if any, to the number of neutrons in a nucleus of the sample that emits a
β^{-} particle.
parts.question_text_latex:
State the change, if any, to the number of neutrons in a nucleus of the sample that emits a
$β^{-}$ particle.

parts.label: (b)
parts.question_text:
The number of β^{-} particles passing a fixed point in the beam in a time of 2.0 minutes is
9.8 × 10^{10}.
Calculate the current, in pA, produced by the beam of β^{-} particles.
current = pA
parts.question_text_latex:
The number of $β^{-}$ particles passing a fixed point in the beam in a time of 2.0 minutes is
$9.8 \times 10^{10}$.
Calculate the current, in pA, produced by the beam of $β^{-}$ particles.
$current = pA $

parts.label: (c)
parts.question_text: Suggest why the β^{-} particles are emitted with a range of kinetic energies.
parts.question_text_latex: Suggest why the $β^{-}$ particles are emitted with a range of kinetic energies.
